full_judgment:
15. Mr AF Hassan Ariff, the learned Senior Advocate with Mr Omar Sadat the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that upon thorough consideration of the judgment and order dated 21-7-2002 passed by this Hon'ble Court in writ petition No.1953 of 1996 the Appellate Division vide judgment and order dated 26-4-2011, passed in Civil Appeal No.70 of 2004, has adjudicated the rate of VAT applicable for SPC electric poles manufactures by determining their status in the eye of law and thereby has imposed the liability of payment of unpaid VAT at the rate of 15% for the disputed period i.e., from18-3-1993 to 31-1-1996. Accordingly, he submits that any purported demand of VAT from 31-3-1996 on wards (as made by the respondent No.4 vide the impugned demand notice dated 22-6-2020 (Annexure-A) is not only misconceived but also barred by limitation as per section 55 of the VAT Act, 1991. He also submits that as on June, 2019 the closing balance of both "মূসক-১৯” Form and Current Register (মূসক-১৮) of the petitioner company clearly showed an amount of Taka 11,08,97,522. In this regard, he submits that the duty to adjust the dues with the current register of the petitioner company lies with the respondents, but with malafide intention they refrained from adjusting the same just to make illegal demand from the petitioner company. 

 25. He also submits that the impugned demand notice dated 20-6-2020 is evidently the continuation of the earlier proceedings and that on every occasion the process of the said proceedings were haulted due to pending proceedings being initiated by the petitioner on different plea. As such, the claim of the petitioner that the same is barred by limitation in view of section 55 of the Act, 1991 is absolutely preposterous and hence, not tenable in the eye of law. 

 36. Subsequently, the NBR in its 5th Board meeting dated 26-12-2019(Annexure-A-1) unanimously took decision to cancel the resolution taken in the meeting held on 01-3- 2015(Annexure-A-3). Consequent thereto the respondent No.4 vide order dated 22-6-2020 (Annexure-A) issued demand notice upon the petitioner under section 56 of the Act,1991 in continuation of the notice dated 20-6-2013, 11-12-2013 (Annexure-E to the writ petition), 14-7-2014 (Annexure-K of writ petition No.6938 of 2014), 21-7-2014 (Annexure-F of the instant writ petition) and 7-9-2014 (Annexure-G of the instant writ petition) respectively, all under section 56 of the Act, 1991 for payment of unpaid VAT to the tune of Taka 21,76,01,590 with direction to deposit the said amount in the government treasury within the prescribed period. In default, to face consequences as provided under section 56 of the Act. Considering the above stated facts, we have no manner of doubt to find that question of limitation under section 55(1) of the Act of 1991, as has been alleged by the petitioner, is not attracted in the present context of the case.
